Track A · Replication + extension

Understand the school-departure finding.

Explore the group rates, the difference between program effects, and the uncertainty—all from the same verified data.

Recommended revised scope: departure from the original NFE × baseline writing. The direct difference is +21.1 percentage points: p=.004, adjusted p=.012. Keep transfer destinations secondary and the observation limits explicit.
✓Original raw data only✓Paper + appendix checkedOriginality is distinct from statistical strength

Which scope is supported by the data

A new regression is not enough when its substantive story is already in the paper. The two rejected directions remain here so you can see why the recommendation changed.

DirectionWhat it addsWork still neededMain risk

Learning: meaningful but inconclusive

Does the randomized program’s effect on learning vary with the baseline score of the teacher? This is a specific new treatment-effect comparison, not a generic attendance-to-learning claim.

Recommended: a question about school departure

Does the program’s effect on departure from the original school differ by initial writing ability? This interaction survives the reported 5% statistical checks, with explicit measurement limits.

Choose by substantive interest and defensible inference. Statistical significance is neither guaranteed nor a sound rule for selecting among explored questions.

What has now been verified

The data search is largely done. The workspace contains the openICPSR replication package, the original Stata programs and their archived outputs, plus Python exploration and a teacher-score dashboard. The publisher links to this same repository.

An independent Python calculation in this review reproduced the main Table 2 result from raw data: +20.7 percentage points (school-clustered SE 3.0), using 3,071 visits in 113 schools. The three period estimates and teacher-score subgroup estimates also matched the archived Stata results. This does not certify every existing extension model. This review also reproduced the learning Table 9A/B coefficients, clustered standard errors and observation counts at the replication package’s reported precision, and rebuilt all Table 10 transition/departure outcomes from the released roster records. Small learning-model R-squared differences are documented. Added interactions remain exploratory and subject to missing-data and measurement limitations.

The randomized treatment combines camera monitoring and attendance-linked pay. These directions estimate effects of that package; they cannot separate the camera effect from the pay effect.

Audited scope: full original article (including footnotes), official eight-page web appendix, one-page erratum, and targeted searches of the supplied code/logs. We did not find the two exact added comparisons; we cannot certify absence from unpublished work or the wider literature.

What to avoid calling new: the teacher-score median split and catch-up story (Table 2 and p. 1250), overall persistence (Table 2), the attendance distribution (Figure 2), and learning splits by child gender or baseline writing ability (Table 9) already appear in the paper.

How these options fit your course

The seminar instructions allow a subgroup analysis, a different outcome, a persistence question, a clearer figure, or a stability check. Only the two surviving questions meet your stricter novelty screen. The original attendance result remains useful background, and each candidate now has its own outcome-table replication.

The final-paper instructions emphasize one central point, with roughly 20–30% devoted to replication and 60–70% to the extension. A result that weakens the original finding is still a result. You do not need to promise a statistically significant finding to choose a worthwhile question.

When you decide: agree on one outcome, one main comparison and a small set of checks before running further exploratory models. Earlier exploration cannot be presented as preregistered. Confirm that the proposed scope satisfies the instructor’s approval requirement.

Document note: the final-paper PDFs state October 15, 2026 at midnight; the earlier seminar handout refers to the registrar. This is the date in the supplied documents, not a live registrar check. Formatting details also differ; use the final checklist and resolve any remaining ambiguity before submission.
